rows.title: Bank of Canada staying cautious but considering more rate hikes: summary
rows.summary: On Nov. 10 the Bank of Canada released its summary of deliberations, showing the governing council believes it may need to raise interest rates again but will move carefully, deciding one meeting at a time. In October the bank lifted its policy rate by a quarter point to 2.5%, its first increase since 2023, to reduce the risk that persistently high oil prices linked to the Middle East war turn into lasting, broad-based inflation. Council members agreed that monetary policy cannot lower global energy prices, but it can stop those costs from spreading to other goods and services. The bank now expects annual inflation to reach 3.5% by the end of 2026 and to stay above 3% for much of 2027. Its surveys suggest businesses still plan to pass some higher costs on to consumers over the next year.
rows.fact: The summary says the outlook is very uncertain because of the Middle East war, Canada-U.S. trade relations, global financial conditions and how quickly higher costs reach consumer prices. The bank says it will look through the direct effect of energy prices but will not let them become broad and persistent inflation. The next scheduled rate decision is Dec. 9.
rows.outlook: The bank expects inflation to stay above 3% for much of 2027 and says further rate increases may be needed.
rows.why: 중앙은행이 유가 같은 '공급 충격'이 물가 전반으로 번지지 않게 하려고 왜 금리를 올리는지, 그리고 그 결정 과정이 어떻게 공개되는지 배울 수 있는 좋은 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: It is a clear real-world case of why a central bank raises interest rates to stop a supply shock like high oil prices from spreading into overall inflation, and of how it explains its reasoning in public.
rows.term_def: The key interest rate a central bank sets to guide what banks charge for loans. Raising it makes borrowing more expensive, which cools spending and inflation.
rows.note: Checked against the Bank of Canada's official Summary of Governing Council deliberations for the Oct. 28, 2026 decision (released Nov. 10), which confirms the 2.5% rate, the 3.5% end-2026 inflation forecast and the meeting-by-meeting approach.

opinion.title: The Bank Raised Rates as Expected but It's Unlikely to Be One and Done
opinion.author: Randall Bartlett and LJ Valencia
opinion.summary: Desjardins economists review the Oct. 28 decision that the new summary of deliberations explains. They say the 25-basis-point hike to 2.50% was almost fully expected, and that the real surprise was the bank's much higher inflation forecast of about 3.4% by end-2026, up from 2.4% in July, driven mostly by oil prices staying high for longer. They point to a more resilient economy but expect fourth-quarter growth to slow to about 0.8% on renewed trade tensions. They call the bank's tone noticeably more hawkish and expect one more hike before the tightening cycle ends. (Written before the Nov. 10 summary, about the same decision.)
opinion.why: 전문 이코노미스트가 중앙은행 발표에서 금리 결정보다 '전망 수정'이 왜 더 중요한지, 그리고 시장이 다음 움직임을 어떻게 예측하는지 보여 줍니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how professional economists read a central bank decision: why the forecast revision can matter more than the rate move itself, and how they predict the next step.

rows.title: Consumer prices increased 0.4% in October, higher than expected
rows.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected, after a 0.6% rise in September. Shelter prices rose 0.3%, and energy rose 0.7% after jumping 5.2% in September, when gasoline costs linked to the Iran war pushed prices up. No annual rate was published for October because the BLS collected no data in October 2025 during the government shutdown; the latest annual figure, 3.7% for September, is well above the Fed's 2% target. The report adds pressure on the Federal Reserve, which held rates steady at its last meeting after a quarter-point hike in September, and markets put the odds of another quarter-point hike in December at about 82%.
rows.fact: October CPI rose 0.4% from September, above the 0.3% forecast. The official BLS release shows core CPI (excluding food and energy) up 0.3% and food up 0.5%. Gas prices have since fallen below $4 a gallon, but that relief is not in the October numbers.
rows.outlook: Markets see about an 82% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December, and the article notes that rate hikes usually take several months to slow inflation.
rows.why: 물가 상승률이 예상보다 높게 나오면 중앙은행이 금리를 올리고 국채 금리와 대출 금리도 함께 오르는 과정을 실제 사례로 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: It shows, with a real case, how a hotter-than-expected inflation report can push a central bank toward raising rates and lift bond yields and borrowing costs.
rows.term_def: A government measure of the average change in prices households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, such as food, gas, rent and medical care.
rows.note: ABC News staff report (Max Zahn). Headline, core, food, energy and shelter figures checked against the BLS October 2026 CPI release (Nov. 10, 8:30 a.m. ET; 12-month changes not published).

opinion.title: Reaction roundup: Experts, analysts weigh in on October CPI report
opinion.author: Anuron Mitra
opinion.summary: This roundup gathers economists' and strategists' reactions to the October CPI report. Schwab's Kevin Gordon and LPL Financial's Jeffrey Roach say the data support a December rate hike, and Pantheon's Samuel Tombs says a half-point move is now under consideration, though he expects most Fed officials to prefer going gradually. Brookings' Robin Brooks calls the reading backward-looking because October was the peak of an oil-price shock, while Roach argues part of the inflation comes from demand, not only from Middle East supply problems.
opinion.why: 같은 물가 지표를 두고 전문가들이 공급 충격과 수요 압력을 어떻게 다르게 해석하는지 비교하며 경제 분석의 관점 차이를 배울 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: It lets students compare how experts read the same inflation data differently, as a supply shock or as demand pressure, and what each view means for the Fed.

rows.title: Korea Targets K-Shaped Divide, Expands Growth Forecasts to Three a Year
rows.summary: At an emergency economic ministers' meeting on Nov. 11, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said narrowing the 'K-shaped divide' will be the central goal of 2027 economic policy. The divide describes how low- and middle-income households and smaller firms have been left out of a recovery driven by the chip boom. Lee will lead a new government-wide task force with five working groups covering the labor market's dual structure and gaps between industries, regions, generations and social groups, which start work on Nov. 12 and must deliver fiscal, tax, financial and regulatory packages by year-end. The government also said it will publish growth forecasts three times a year instead of twice, the first change in 32 years, and extend the temporary fuel tax cut through Jan. 31, 2027.
rows.fact: Temporary and contract workers at large companies earned 61.1% of permanent employees' wages last year, down from 69.1% in 2021. Net assets of people aged 60 and over were 2.14 times those of people in their 30s, up from 1.47 times in 2020. The chip-centered electronics industry created 2.87 jobs per 1 billion won of final demand, less than a third of the 9.5 jobs created by services.
rows.outlook: The task force's measures are due by the end of 2026 for the December growth strategy, and the three-forecasts-a-year system starts in 2027.
rows.why: 반도체 호황 속에서도 왜 성장의 혜택이 고르게 퍼지지 않는지, 그리고 정부가 재정·세제·규제 정책으로 그 격차에 어떻게 대응하려는지 실제 사례로 배울 수 있는 기사입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows with real data why a chip-led boom does not spread its benefits evenly, and how a government tries to respond to that gap with fiscal, tax and regulatory policy.
rows.term_def: A recovery in which some groups, such as big exporters and wealthier households, do much better while others, such as small firms and low-income households, stagnate or fall behind, like the two arms of the letter K.
rows.note: New policy announcement of Nov. 11, not repeat coverage of the gap itself. Task force and forecast-frequency change cross-checked with Yonhap reports carried by The Korea Times (Nov. 11). Seoul Economic Daily says its English article was AI-translated from Korean.

opinion.title: Lee's Vision of 'Growth for All' Hinges on Structural Reform, Not Spending
opinion.author: Editorial Board
opinion.summary: The editorial responds to President Lee Jae-myung's call to move from 'growth for the few' to 'growth for all' in his address on the 820.9 trillion won 2027 budget. It backs the goal of easing polarization but argues that fiscal expansion alone cannot sustain growth and pushes costs onto future generations. It notes that a planned 162.3 trillion won future response fund relies partly on one-off chip-boom tax revenue, yet 21.2 trillion won of next year's fund spending is expected to recur every year. It urges structural reforms instead, such as easing labor regulations and fixing the labor market's dual structure. (Written before the Nov. 11 task force, on the same polarization agenda.)
opinion.why: 양극화를 줄이려면 돈을 더 쓰는 것(재정 확대)과 구조개혁 중 무엇이 중요한지, 일시적 세수로 영구 지출을 하면 어떤 위험이 있는지 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It lets students weigh spending more against structural reform as ways to reduce inequality, and see the risk of paying for permanent programs with temporary tax revenue.

rows.title: 'A task of historic proportions': Economic experts warn government of future budget troubles
rows.summary: On Nov. 11 Germany's Council of Economic Experts, the government's statutory advisory panel, handed Chancellor Friedrich Merz its annual report and raised its growth forecasts to 1.3% for 2026 and 1.0% for 2027, citing recovery from the energy price shock and rising exports and orders. It warned that public debt, now 63.5% of GDP, would climb to about 98% by 2040 if defence spending above 1% of GDP keeps being exempted from the debt brake. It proposed phasing out loan-financed defence spending from 2031 by raising that 1% threshold step by step. It also called for cutting subsidies, adopting the pension commission's proposals, reversing a planned pension top-up for mothers and trimming tax privileges such as joint taxation of spouses. Even then, a financing gap of 2.4% of GDP would remain in 2040, so tax rises may be needed in the medium term.
rows.fact: The council's spring forecasts had been only 0.5% growth for 2026 and 0.8% for 2027, so this is a large upgrade. Under its proposed path, debt would peak at about 87% of GDP in 2037. Council chair Monika Schnitzer called a limit on federal spending growth unavoidable.
rows.outlook: The government is still negotiating how to finance the 2027 budget ahead of a final budget committee session on Nov. 12.
rows.why: 경기가 좋아지는 시기에도 국방비 같은 지출을 빚으로 계속 메우면 국가부채가 쌓인다는 점을 보여 주어, 재정정책의 지속가능성과 세대 간 부담이라는 원리를 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: It shows that even while the economy is improving, paying for spending such as defence with borrowing makes national debt pile up, teaching how sustainable fiscal policy works and how its costs are shared between generations.
rows.term_def: When a government cuts spending and/or raises taxes so it borrows less and its debt stops growing faster than the economy.
rows.note: Original German headline translated. Growth figures cross-checked with ZDFheute and Reuters (Nov. 11). The council advises the government; its proposals are recommendations, not government decisions.

opinion.title: Companies warn the economic upturn will be a flash in the pan
opinion.author: Thomas Burgert; expert view from IW economist Michael Grömling
opinion.summary: This report presents expert commentary from Michael Grömling of the business-funded German Economic Institute (IW), published hours before the council's report. Citing an October IW survey of about 1,000 firms, he argues the upswing will fade next year and calls it a short-lived 'flash in the pan', noting that firms' expectations have been negative for their longest stretch since 2005. In the survey 32% of firms expect job cuts next year and 39% plan to invest less, and IW forecasts growth of 1.2% this year and just under 1% next year. Grömling says Germany should not count on help from abroad and should carry out its planned reforms. (Original German headline translated.)
opinion.why: 정부 지출과 수출로 생긴 일시적 경기 회복과 민간 투자에 기반한 지속적 성장의 차이를 기업 설문 자료로 생각해 볼 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: Using business survey data, it helps students think about the difference between a temporary recovery driven by government spending and exports and lasting growth built on private investment.

rows.title: China's trade surplus surpasses $1 trillion for a 2nd straight year, as exports surge 35%
rows.summary: China's customs data released Nov. 10 showed October exports up 35.2% from a year earlier, while imports rose even faster at 41.6%. That pushed the January-October trade surplus to $1.04 trillion, the second straight year above $1 trillion, putting China on track to beat 2025's record $1.2 trillion. The October surplus itself narrowed to $105.3 billion from $133.5 billion in September as imports picked up, with semiconductor exports jumping 137.1% and auto exports rising 37.6%. Economists cited overcapacity, high domestic savings and weak domestic demand as drivers, and warned that EU measures, U.S. tariffs or an AI-industry slowdown could hurt exports. Trade is expected to be a major topic at next week's Trump-Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen.
rows.fact: January-October surplus reached $1.04 trillion; October exports rose 35.2% and imports 41.6% year on year. For January-October, the surplus with the U.S. was about $266.5 billion and with the EU more than $310 billion.
rows.outlook: China is expected to set a new annual surplus record in 2026, but the U.S.-China trade truce runs only until January.
rows.why: 한 나라가 수출은 많이 하고 국내 소비는 약할 때 무역흑자가 왜 커지는지, 그리고 이것이 왜 다른 나라와의 무역 갈등으로 이어지는지 보여 주는 사례입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how strong exports combined with weak domestic consumption create a huge trade surplus, and why that surplus leads to trade friction with other countries.
rows.term_def: The amount by which the value of a country's exports exceeds the value of its imports over a period.
rows.note: Figures cross-checked with an ING Think note (Nov. 10), which confirms the export, import, chip and auto growth rates; ING's body text gives the October surplus as $104.5 billion, so the AP figure is used.

opinion.title: Why China's $1 trillion trade surplus isn't all good news for its economy
opinion.author: John Power
opinion.summary: The piece argues that the record surplus shows China's export strength but hides a lopsided economy: households save a third or more of their income, and household consumption is only about 39% of GDP versus 68% in the U.S. It blames a thin social safety net, a slumping property market and an undervalued currency. Economists including Bruegel's Alicia Garcia Herrero say export dependence cannot last because other countries will raise barriers, as the EU did by capping Chinese hybrid car imports. Beijing's consumption-focused five-year plan has delivered only modest results so far, with retail sales up just 1.1% in September.
opinion.why: 무역흑자가 무조건 좋은 것이 아니라 소비·저축·사회안전망의 불균형을 드러낼 수 있다는 점을 거시경제 관점에서 생각해 보게 합니다.
opinion.why_en: It challenges the idea that a trade surplus is always good, linking it to imbalances in consumption, saving and the social safety net from a macroeconomic perspective.
